title: Storing tokens safely in the browser

videos.script:
Lesson 5 gave the planner a server, and the browser a cookie. {{cookie}} Today's question is where a secret should live in a browser.

There are six places. {{six}} Only one of them keeps the secret from the page's own scripts: a cookie marked HttpOnly. You test that in Chromium. A script on the page finds the cookie empty, and finds a token in local storage at once.

Then the server's half. {{server}} Three tests ask it what the browser cannot. Is the cookie marked properly? Does signing out end the login? Does a login end on its own? All three fail.

You fix the server, and they pass. {{green}}

Last, apps that hold real tokens from a provider. {{bff}} The safest place for those is a small server of your own, and the page never sees them.
